semantic_correction.stem: A client is preoccupied with a slight or unnoticeable perceived flaw in appearance, repeatedly checks mirrors and seeks reassurance, and has substantial social impairment. Which condition is most consistent with this presentation?

options.A: Obsessive-compulsive disorder, because repetitive checking identifies OCD even when the central preoccupation is a slight or unobservable appearance flaw.
options.B: Social anxiety disorder, because social impairment from fear of others’ reactions is sufficient even when the central concern is a perceived appearance flaw.
options.C: Illness anxiety disorder, because repeated reassurance seeking about appearance indicates fear of serious disease rather than concern about appearance itself.
options.D: Body dysmorphic disorder, because a slight or unobservable appearance flaw is paired with repetitive checking or reassurance seeking and significant impairment.

semantic_correction.rationale: D is correct. The current NCBI Bookshelf StatPearls review summarizes DSM-5-TR body dysmorphic disorder criteria as preoccupation with one or more perceived appearance defects or flaws that are not observable or are only slight to others, repetitive behaviors or mental acts in response to the concern, and clinically significant distress or impairment; the appearance concern must also not be better explained by an eating disorder. Mirror checking and reassurance seeking are characteristic repetitive behaviors described in the review. A is incorrect because repetitive checking can occur in BDD and does not by itself make OCD the better classification when the preoccupation is specifically a perceived appearance defect. B is incorrect because social impairment can result from BDD; the defining pattern here is the appearance-flaw preoccupation plus repetitive appearance-related behaviors. C is incorrect because illness anxiety disorder centers on fear of having or acquiring serious illness rather than a perceived appearance defect. The item asks for the condition most consistent with the presentation rather than asserting a complete formal diagnosis from a brief vignette.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Recognize body dysmorphic disorder by the combination of preoccupation with slight or unobservable perceived appearance flaws, repetitive appearance-related behaviors, and clinically significant distress or impairment.
semantic_correction.source_version_date: StatPearls 2026 edition; chapter last updated January 20, 2024; current NCBI Bookshelf page accessed August 22, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Introduction and Body Dysmorphic Disorder DSM-5-TR Criteria, current web lines 93 and 128–136: preoccupation with perceived physical defects/flaws not observable or only slight to others; repetitive behaviors; clinically significant distress or impairment; appearance concern not better explained by an eating disorder. Introduction also identifies mirror checking, grooming, skin picking, camouflaging, comparison, and reassurance-seeking as common repetitive behaviors.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: The presentation of slight or unobservable perceived appearance flaws, repetitive mirror checking/reassurance seeking, and significant impairment is most consistent with body dysmorphic disorder.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests a canonical BDD presentation with one clearly best answer, balanced option lengths, current DSM-5-TR alignment, and no answer-length cue.

option_audit.A: Incorrect. Repetitive checking is not specific to OCD, and the appearance-defect focus plus repetitive appearance-related behavior and impairment fit BDD more directly.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Social impairment is present, but the central appearance-flaw preoccupation and repetitive checking/reassurance pattern are characteristic of BDD rather than primary social anxiety disorder.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Illness anxiety disorder centers on fear of serious illness; the stem centers on perceived appearance defects.
option_audit.D: Correct. The stem directly matches the core DSM-5-TR BDD features summarized in the current StatPearls review.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. D uniquely integrates the appearance-defect preoccupation, repetitive appearance-related behaviors, and major impairment; the other options each mismatch the central content of the preoccupation.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel diagnostic explanations with nearly identical length and specificity; the prior uniquely-long correct response was eliminated and no conspicuous absolute-word pattern identifies the key.
